proposal.text: Q1: src/hub.ts:65 sets `DEFAULT_NUDGE_MS = Number(process.env.CHATROOM_NUDGE_AFTER_MS ?? 180_000)` (applied at hub.ts:94; persistence fallback hub/persistence.ts:77). Verdict: keep 3 min for a nine-seat session. (a) The silence nudge armNudge (hub.ts:1036-1059) re-arms on every post (hub.ts:985) and posts an identical nudge at most twice (:1054), so in a busy nine-seat room it seldom fires, and when it fires it signals a real stall. (b) The openings deadline (2 periods at creation hub.ts:136, 1 period after the first opening hub.ts:1081, plus one warning period if a seat never joined hub.ts:1093-1108) is the main risk for nine seats: slow joiners can miss the reveal. But the reveal never blocks chat, and late seats can still speak (server.ts:325, :442), so a longer default would hold eight seats to wait for one. Keep it, with the env override for slow fleets. Q2: only 'bench-build-oracle-audit.test.ts' appears more than once in offlineScripts (scripts/offline-runner.mjs:64 and :78). Q3: MAX_WAIT_MS = 55_000 at src/server.ts:21, comment "stay under typical MCP client tool timeouts (Codex 60s)", enforced at server.ts:348 (zod max) and :359. Still justified: the hub's own seats raise their client timeouts (codex-seat.ts:13 tool_timeout_sec=120, env.ts:35 MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT=120000, seat.ts:417-418 timeout 180_000), but external MCP clients keep the ~60s default, and wait() wakes on events (server.ts:20), so the cap costs no latency.

But the reveal never blocks chat, and late seats can still speak (hub.ts:1049 "Chat is open meanwhile", hub.ts:1107 reveal note "who can still speak in chat"; the minutes are surfaced in hints at server.ts:325, :442, :464), Tradeoff: the reveal is immediate once everyone has submitted (hub.ts:1082-1083), so a longer period costs time only when a seat is slow. But after a reveal, submit_opening throws (hub.ts:1074), so a slow ninth seat permanently loses its independent opening and joins anchored. With nine seats that risk is real. It is bounded, though: the clock starts only at the first opening (:1081), a seat that never joined gets a warning plus one more period (:1099-1104), and the late seat still contributes in chat. A longer default costs every slow-seat room minutes of idle waiting. On balance keep 3 min; fleets with slow cold starts should raise it via the env override. Keep it, with the env override for slow fleets. Q2: only 'bench-build-oracle-audit.test.ts' appears more than once in offlineScripts (scripts/offline-runner.mjs:64 and :78). seat-env-regression.ts and claude-lean-flags-regression.ts recur in the file only through the --experimental-vm-modules conditional in offlineCommands (offline-runner.mjs:192), not in the list. Q3: MAX_WAIT_MS = 55_000 at src/server.ts:21, comment "stay under typical MCP client tool timeouts (Codex 60s)", enforced at server.ts:348 (zod max) and :359. Still justified: the hub's own seats raise their client timeouts (codex-seat.ts:13 tool_timeout_sec=120, env.ts:35 MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT=120000, seat.ts:417-418 timeout 180_000), but external MCP clients keep the ~60s default, and wait() wakes on events (server.ts:20), so the cap costs no latency.
